Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

onepagr 0.2.0

This release folds in fixes from two external code reviews and a round of accessibility evidence work. Apart from the header subtitle change described under Themes, all 15 built-in template and theme combinations render the same as before these fixes (same text, same pixels).

Data and tokens

  • compile_typst() and render_onepager() escape a double quote, backslash or newline in a value that a template places inside a quoted string (organization names, alt text, contact details, file paths), so Sample "North" Health Department renders instead of failing in Typst. A value in the body of a template is still Typst markup, as before.
  • typst_escape() is new. It makes plain text safe for a body token: #, $, *, _, a backtick, <, >, @, /, brackets and ~ show up literally. Escaping the slash keeps // in the text from starting a Typst comment, which would drop the rest of the line.
  • compile_typst() reports a lone ] or an unclosed [ in a body value in R, naming the token, instead of as a Typst error about a generated file. The check runs after defaults and references are filled in, so a bracket that arrives through either is caught too.
  • A token in a // comment of a template no longer receives its value. A value with a newline in it used to end the comment and turn the rest of the line into live markup, which could add a page.
  • A default can refer to an optional token declared below it, and a chain of references (a refers to b, b refers to c) is followed to the end. Defaults or values that refer to each other in a loop are an error. Only {{{token}}} references are filled in; a {{name}} or {{#section}} in a value stays literal text.
  • A name that one of your values refers to is no longer reported as ignored. A missing token at the end of a chain of references (a refers to b, b refers to c, and there is no value for c) is reported by name instead of rendering blank.
  • One data list can still be shared across templates: a value that only another template uses is not resolved, so a reference loop among those values no longer stops this render.
  • A double-brace {{name}}, a {{#section}} or a stray {{ in the comment text of a template is neutralized as well, not only the triple-brace form.
  • An error about a missing token names the built-in template, such as cohort_summary, not template.typ.
  • Numbers are formatted without scientific notation, so 100000 prints as 100000, not 1e+05. A number with more digits than a short decimal, an R logical, or a vector longer than one is an error that points to fmt_n() and fmt_pct() or to the accepted spelling.
  • A value that refers to a token ({{{n_total}}}), including a value from template_data(tokens = "optional"), is filled from your data, so literal {{{token}}} text no longer reaches the PDF.
  • template_tokens() gains a needed_by column, and extract_required_tokens() lists only tokens the template body uses. A token that only an optional token’s default uses is needed only while that default is in use.
  • validate_template_data() warns about a blank required value. A template can declare // allow-empty: token for text that is blank on purpose; the alert templates do this for cluster_text and resources_text.
  • Template parsing no longer treats a // after a URL or inside a quoted string as a comment, so a token after https:// on a line is found. A token name with a dot is rejected, template_tokens("name") no longer prefers a file of the same name in the working directory, and each template is parsed once per session (the file is only re-read to notice edits).
  • A *_width bar token must be a plain number from 0 to 100, and bars are clamped to their track. "65%", "64,6" and "140" stop with an error naming the token.
  • compile_typst() no longer crashes on a custom template with no tokens when data has a name it does not use.
  • Every template takes an optional doc_lang (default "en") that sets the document language screen readers use.

Export, render and install

  • export_template() stops if dest already holds an exported template, so hand edits are not lost; use overwrite = TRUE to replace it. It also takes theme_path.
  • render_onepager() stops on an extra_assets file that would replace theme.typ, components.typ or a template file, or that two assets share a name, and stops on a failed file copy. It replaces its _typst work folder on each render, but only one that onepagr created (it holds a hidden marker file). Any other folder at that path, including an export_template() copy or a work folder left by an earlier version, is left alone and the render stops, so delete an old one once.
  • The documentation for render_onepager() and compile_typst() now says that template_rendered.typ, not template.typ, is the file that compiles.
  • render_onepager() checks the data before it creates the output folder or replaces the work folder, so a data error no longer removes the previous render’s work folder or leaves a new empty folder behind.
  • install_quarto() finds bin/quarto wherever the archive put it (the macOS archive has no quarto-<version>/ folder) and downloads the arm64 build on 64-bit ARM Linux. set_quarto_path() saves an absolute path.
  • install_quarto() asks before the download in an interactive session, and after installing it removes the older copies it put in its folder, so the folder does not grow with every version. A copy that QUARTO_PATH points into (in this session, or in the home or working-directory .Renviron) is kept, and so is anything the function did not create.
  • A QUARTO_PATH that names a file that is not there stops with a message that says so, before the previous PDF is replaced, instead of “error in running command” after it has been deleted.

Themes

  • check_theme() no longer fails a theme for lacking brand-sky, card-bg, callout-bg, lessons-bg or disclaimer-bg, which no component reads, and reports unknown theme-grad keys as unknown_grad.
  • Callout body text is a theme key, callout-text, with the previous color as its fallback, so a custom theme with a dark callout background can set it.
  • The header subtitle in all five templates is now solid white instead of white at 85% opacity. With the default theme the translucent text measured 3.93:1 against the lightest end of the header gradient, under the 4.5:1 that WCAG 2.2 AA requires for text this size. It now measures 4.95:1 there, the same margin as the title, and the uk and kdph themes pass by a wider margin (7.53:1 and 10.60:1).

Accessibility documentation

  • vignette("accessibility-checks") is new. It explains what PAC, veraPDF and Typst’s own ua-1 compile check, which PDF/UA-1 conditions still need a person (cross-referenced to the PDF Association’s Matterhorn Protocol 1.1), and gives a checklist for them.
  • The README states the scope of the accessibility claims: which checkers were run, that PAC was run by hand, and that onepagr does not certify legal compliance with any law or regulation. Every built-in template and theme was also checked with veraPDF (PDF/UA-1 profile).
  • The README and the accessibility vignette now say that on the two alert templates the page footer is a pagination artifact, so its logos, organization name and contact details are not read by a screen reader.

Documentation and packaging

  • fmt_n() and fmt_pct() document that a half rounds to the even digit.
  • example_data() names the missing file when a template has no example. Templates are read and written as UTF-8.
  • DESCRIPTION now says the templates are designed to meet WCAG 2.2 level AA and PDF/UA-1, quotes ‘Typst’, spells out both acronyms, adds the copyright holder role to Authors@R, declares R (>= 4.1.0) and quarto (>= 1.5.0) (the first quarto release that exports quarto_available(), which needs R 4.1.0), and lists stats in Imports.
  • example_data("county_choropleth") can be rendered: its five placeholder maps ship in inst/extdata/maps, and the help page shows how to pass them as extra_assets.
  • citation() takes its year from the package’s publication date, so it no longer changes every January.
  • Tests and vignettes that render a PDF run only when check_quarto() reports a Quarto whose bundled Typst is new enough, so an older Quarto skips them instead of failing.
  • The bundled header texture is an original generated pattern, and the bundled Fluent icon in the hex logo is credited in inst/COPYRIGHTS.
  • The README gains a Background section on where the templates came from, and the gallery images are regenerated from the current templates and themes.
  • Corrected references to unshipped design documents and to theme keys that do not exist.

Internal

  • check_theme() and compile_typst() are split into smaller helpers, the “Quarto was not found” error comes from one place, and render_onepager() inherits parameter documentation from export_template() and compile_typst(). A .lintr file sets the lint settings, and a lint workflow runs on every push.

onepagr 0.1.0

Initial release. onepagr generates polished, WCAG 2.2 AA and PDF/UA-1 accessible one-page (front-and-back) PDF reports from analysis output, using a small set of fixed Typst templates and a design-token theme system that a consuming project can restyle with its own branding.

Core API

  • render_onepager(): render a named list of values to a finished, accessible PDF using a built-in template and theme.
  • export_template(): copy a built-in template’s full source into your own project for exploration or hand-editing.
  • compile_typst(): low-level primitive underlying both of the above; compiles any .typ file with whisker-substituted data.
  • check_quarto() / install_quarto(): detect and, on request, install the Quarto/Typst toolchain onepagr depends on.
  • list_templates() / list_themes() / resolve_template() / resolve_theme(): the built-in template and theme registry.
  • fmt_n() / fmt_pct(): number-formatting helpers matching the convention every built-in template’s tokens expect.
  • Logos are data, not template edits: every template takes a primary logo (always shown) plus two optional partner logos, off by default and switched on independently with show_partner_a/show_partner_b. A single organization passes only logo_primary_path and logo_primary_alt (the header texture defaults to the bundled one); a two-agency partnership and a three-organization lockup are first-class cases too. Switching a partner on without its path and alt text is an error, not a placeholder.
  • render_onepager()’s font_dir argument makes a directory of font files available to Typst for a compile, for a theme font that isn’t installed system-wide.
  • A template can declare a token optional with a comment line, // optional-token: name = default. When the data list omits that token, compile_typst() and render_onepager() use the default instead of raising a missing-token error, and extract_required_tokens() no longer lists it.
  • All the reader-facing text in the built-in templates is tokenized, so changing it is a change to your data list, not to the template: section headings, box labels, captions, paragraphs, bullets, bar-chart row labels, the metadata strip and footer labels, and chart and map alt text. Each token is optional and defaults to the text the template shipped with, so default output is unchanged. Names follow a prefix pattern (heading_*, label_*, stat_*, bar_*, text_*, alt_*, and a few others; see the theming vignette, Part 5). A default may refer to other tokens, as in Results (N = {{{n_total}}}), and those stay required.
  • A name in data that no template uses is ignored with a warning instead of silently, and the warning suggests the closest token when there is one ("heading_glnce" was ignored ... Did you mean "heading_glance"?). A name that belongs to a different built-in template stays quiet, so one data list can be shared across templates.
  • template_tokens() lists every token a built-in template, or an exported copy of one, takes: which are required, and the default of each optional one.
  • template_data() returns a complete, working starter list for a built-in template: every token render_onepager() would read, each already set to a real value, not a blank to guess the shape of. A required token (which has no default of its own) gets the matching value from the template’s example_data(); an optional token gets its own shipped default. The tokens argument narrows this to "required" or "optional" alone, and the result’s "required" attribute names which entries came from which, so the plain list itself stays exactly what render_onepager() expects.
  • example_data() returns a built-in template’s full example data as a named list: the same data this package’s own tests render, and the single, installed source of truth that template_data() also draws from, so there’s no separate hand-typed copy to keep in sync.
  • The shared footer’s logo lockup takes a height and a vertical nudge for each logo (logo-a-height, logo-height, logo-b-height and logo-a-dy, logo-dy, logo-b-dy, defaulting to 32pt and 0pt), for logos whose artwork differs in size or sits off-center in its canvas. Every logo sits in a cell as tall as the tallest logo shown (a hidden partner’s height is ignored), so the dividers between logos span the full lockup height.

Templates

Five built-in templates, each a genuinely distinct informational shape:

  • cohort_summary: contrasts two groups at a point in time.
  • trend_snapshot: tracks one metric across several time periods.
  • overdose_spike_alert: anomaly/threshold alert bulletin (ODMAP-style), natural pagination.
  • syndromic_alert: anomaly/threshold alert for any syndrome (ESSENCE-style), natural pagination.
  • county_choropleth: geographic bivariate comparison across counties, supports per-run generated map images via extra_assets. Its footer logos can be sized and nudged per render with the optional tokens logo_a_height, logo_height, logo_b_height (points, default 32) and logo_a_dy, logo_dy, logo_b_dy (points, default 0).

Themes

  • default: a brand-neutral palette built on Bootstrap 5.3’s own color variables.
  • uk: University of Kentucky and Kentucky Injury Prevention and Research Center (KIPRC) branding.
  • kdph: Kentucky Department for Public Health colors and fonts, following the department’s 2026 Data Visualization Style Guidelines (unofficial; not endorsed by KDPH). A theme’s body-font can be a fallback list instead of a single name; kdph uses one (Calibri, then Carlito, then Liberation Sans).

Every theme has three type and spacing keys: min-font-size (a floor for text size), font-scale, and space-scale. All default to no change. Each can be overridden for a single render with the optional data tokens min_font_size (points), font_scale, and space_scale. A custom theme needs the three keys added. Boxes that hold text grow with the type, including the alert templates’ bottom margin and the county map explainer box; images, logos, and map sizes stay fixed. When a fixed-page template’s output no longer matches its designed page count, render_onepager() says so.

Every built-in template combined with the default or uk theme is verified against both Typst’s --pdf-standard ua-1 compile-time check and a real PAC (PDF Accessibility Checker) run covering both the PDF/UA and WCAG tabs. Combinations with kdph compile under --pdf-standard ua-1, have computed WCAG contrast ratios at both ends of every gradient, and were run through PAC on the sample content.
